articles.title: Real-Estate Listing Retrieval with Node.js: Tracing Citations Without Latency Surprises
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use a staged retrieval design with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source context that travels with every result. For a real-estate listing discovery system, citation tracing…
articles.body: Short answer: use a staged retrieval design with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source context that travels with every result. For a real-estate listing discovery system, citation tracing is part of the retrieval contract, not a formatting step added after generation. The bill is usually dominated by work you keep repeating: embedding changed text, searching too many candidates, and reprocessing records that should have been removed. The first useful design question is therefore not “which vector database is fastest?” It is “what is one retrieval unit, and how fresh must it be?” Start with a retrieval contract Write the answer shape before choosing an endpoint.
articles.author: ValdemarBlack3817

articles.title: When an input moves mid-run, vx keeps the result and skips the save
articles.excerpt: A cache key is a promise: these outputs were built from exactly these So when an input moves mid-run, vx keeps the run's result, saves no [vx] app#build: `packages/app/src/routes.gen.ts` changed after…
articles.body: A cache key is a promise: these outputs were built from exactly these inputs. vx takes the key just before the command runs. If an input changes while the command is running, the output was built from bytes the key does not describe, and filing it under that key would replay the wrong output on the next hit. So when an input moves mid-run, vx keeps the run's result, saves no entry, and tells you which file moved: [vx] app#build: `packages/app/src/routes.gen.ts` changed after its key was taken — the result stands, but is not saved under a key that no longer describes it; if the task writes it, declare it in cache.outputs The next run is a miss and builds again from what is on disk now. How it notices After the command, vx checks each input once.

articles.title: I built a tool that answers "what changed?" when production breaks
articles.excerpt: It's 2 AM. PagerDuty goes off. You open your monitoring tool and it tells you, with great confidence, that checkout latency is up 400%. Thanks. Extremely useful. Now the actual work starts: what chang…
articles.body: It's 2 AM. PagerDuty goes off. You open your monitoring tool and it tells you, with great confidence, that checkout latency is up 400%. Thanks. Extremely useful. Now the actual work starts: what changed? You open the deploy history in one tab, the feature-flag dashboard in another, the migration log in a third, Slack in a fourth, and you spend twenty minutes doing timestamp archaeology while the pager keeps screaming. Every on-call knows this drill. The cause is usually a recent change - a deploy, a flag flip, a migration. Finding it is the slow part. I got tired of doing it by hand, so I built LastGood . What it does LastGood ingests your alerts (generic webhook or Datadog), GitHub deploys, DB migrations, and feature-flag flips into one timeline per service.

articles.title: HookSentry CLI: Production-Ready Self-Hosted Webhook Ingestion Proxy, Dead-Letter Queue & Auto-Retry Engine
articles.excerpt: In modern distributed microservices and event-driven architectures, third-party webhooks are the lifeblood of business operations. Payment confirmations from Stripe or Paddle, inventory synchronizatio…
articles.body: In modern distributed microservices and event-driven architectures, third-party webhooks are the lifeblood of business operations. Payment confirmations from Stripe or Paddle, inventory synchronizations from Shopify, identity lifecycle updates from Clerk, and CI/CD triggers from GitHub all rely on asynchronous HTTP callbacks. Yet, raw webhook ingestion is notoriously brittle. When your application server restarts during a blue-green deployment, experiences a database connection pool exhaustion, or hits an unexpected 500 Internal Server Error, incoming webhook payloads are dropped. Most external providers implement crude retry policies—or none at all—causing dropped revenue events, unsynchronized user states, and hours of tedious manual log parsing.

articles.title: Why I Built a $5 ESP32 Hardware Firewall to Stop Cyber-Physical Grid Attacks
articles.excerpt: `The Problem: Physics is Faster Than the CloudAs we rapidly deploy distributed high-voltage infrastructure—like public EV charging stations and autonomous drone landing pads—we are securing them exact…
articles.body: `The Problem: Physics is Faster Than the CloudAs we rapidly deploy distributed high-voltage infrastructure—like public EV charging stations and autonomous drone landing pads—we are securing them exactly the wrong way. The industry standard relies on centralized cloud firewalls and heavy industrial controllers to authorize power delivery.But this creates a fatal vulnerability: Tight Coupling and Latency.If a threat actor breaches the central network and commands a fleet of remote chargers to draw maximum amperage simultaneously, the system relies on the cloud to detect the anomaly, encrypt a response, and send a "kill" command. That round-trip takes hundreds of milliseconds.

articles.title: Rashed Kalantar on Founding MedicApp: Building a UAE Patient-Clinic Platform to Acquisition
articles.excerpt: Back in 2021, I launched MedicApp in the UAE to solve a problem almost everyone recognizes: getting a clinic appointment was harder than it should be. In 2024, the company was acquired. Below is a bre…
articles.body: Back in 2021, I launched MedicApp in the UAE to solve a problem almost everyone recognizes: getting a clinic appointment was harder than it should be. In 2024, the company was acquired. Below is a breakdown of what we built and the reasoning behind it. The starting point Booking care in the UAE often involved calling a clinic, waiting on the line, and keeping your own notes on past visits. Clinics, meanwhile, leaned on word of mouth and ads to fill their schedules. Patients and providers had no shared, simple channel. What we built MedicApp was a CRM designed to connect patients with clinics in one app. The core feature set: One-tap appointments – reserve a clinic visit quickly. Personal visit history – every previous appointment in one place.

articles.title: SpaceX rocket launch creates incredible 'space jellyfish' visible throughout US East Coast (photos)
articles.excerpt: The SpaceX cargo launch to the International Space Station on Tuesday morning (Oct. 13) created a dazzling display seen up and down the US East Coast.
articles.body: Rockets are launching to space on a near-daily basis these days, but short of livestreaming a liftoff from the comfort of your Wi-Fi router, relatively few spectators are in the right place and time to see one with their own eyes. That wasn't the case Tuesday morning (Oct. 13), when SpaceX launched the CRS-35 mission for NASA . A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT), carrying a cargo variant of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft on the company's 35th commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station (ISS). Following the northward path of the space station's orbit at the time, the rocket flew a trajectory along the United States' East Coast.

articles.body: Tesla has stopped taking orders for the Model 3 Premium in Canada, the Shanghai-built trim that brought the electric sedan down to $39,490 CAD. The automaker says it has used up its import quota for Chinese-made EVs and doesn’t expect to reopen orders until March 2027. But the Canadian government’s own tracker tells a different story: 33,069 of the 49,000 permits for China-made EVs in the current quota year are still available. more…
